cases.applicability: Applies only when an implementation or migrated state exposes initialization before an authorized transaction; constructor-initialized, locked implementations are outside the model.
cases.attacker: An unprivileged caller who can invoke a public initializer before governance.
cases.guard: Require the governance identity and consume initialization exactly once.
cases.invariant: Only the configured governance identity may initialize an upgraded implementation.
sequence: deploy implementation with an unset owner

cases.applicability: Models systems where proof validity and endpoint identity are separate checks; it does not apply when the verified statement cryptographically commits to the local route.
cases.attacker: A valid sender on an untrusted source route.
cases.control: authenticated source route and message payload
cases.family: cross-chain origin, identity, nonce, and proof binding
cases.guard: Bind authenticated source route and sender to the local endpoint configuration.
cases.invariant: A message authenticated on another route must not release assets for the configured route.
sequence: obtain a valid authentication on route 9
submit it to the route-7 release endpoint

cases.applicability: Applies to at-least-once delivery channels with value-bearing handlers; naturally idempotent handlers or consensus-enforced single delivery are excluded.
cases.attacker: A relayer replaying a previously valid message without privileged keys.
cases.family: cross-chain origin, identity, nonce, and proof binding
cases.guard: Record and reject an authenticated nonce before applying its value transition.
cases.invariant: One authenticated message identifier may create credit at most once.

cases.applicability: Applies when proof verification is detached from semantic binding of decoded fields; typed proofs that include every execution argument are outside the preconditions.
cases.attacker: An unprivileged proof submitter substituting the payout argument.
cases.control: proof, committed recipient, and requested recipient
cases.family: cross-chain origin, identity, nonce, and proof binding
cases.guard: Decode and compare the proof-committed recipient before payout.
cases.invariant: A valid inclusion proof may pay only the recipient committed by its leaf.
sequence: copy a valid victim leaf and proof
submit proof while requesting attacker payout

cases.applicability: The synthetic equality boundary applies to forks that alter or omit an upstream consensus check; it is not a claim about any named client's exact timestamp rule.
cases.attacker: A permissionless block producer proposing a boundary-valued header.
cases.guard: Preserve the upstream strict monotonic-time validation in every fork path.
cases.invariant: A child header whose time does not advance its parent must be rejected.
sequence: propose child timestamp 100 through the forked validator

cases.applicability: Applies to synchronous callback surfaces that expose stale balances; pull-only transfers or pre-committed debits do not meet the model.
cases.attacker: A depositor controlling a callback receiver.
cases.control: callback order and one reentrant attempt
cases.guard: Commit debit and reentrancy state before invoking external callback code.
cases.invariant: A callback cannot withdraw more than the balance that existed at entry.
sequence: callback requests a second withdrawal before accounting settles

cases.applicability: Applies where timeout and acknowledgement may race or be retried; mutually exclusive consensus transitions do not satisfy the ordering precondition.
cases.attacker: A sender controlling timeout timing and late-message relay order.
cases.family: timeout, retry, refund, and recovery reentrancy/idempotency
cases.guard: Use one terminal state shared by refund and acknowledgement transitions.
cases.invariant: A transfer escrow cannot both refund its sender and pay its recipient.

cases.applicability: Applies only to callback-capable recovery payouts with status written after interaction; non-callback assets and checks-effects-interactions implementations are excluded.
cases.attacker: An eligible claimant controlling the payout callback.
cases.control: callback reentry and claim status update order
cases.family: timeout, retry, refund, and recovery reentrancy/idempotency
cases.guard: Mark the claim consumed before executing its payout callback.
cases.invariant: A recovery claim can transfer its allocation no more than once.
sequence: reenter claim once from payout callback

cases.applicability: Applies when signatures can cross execution domains and verification omits a changing domain component; single-domain keys with protocol-enforced separation are excluded.
cases.attacker: A signature holder replaying a valid payload after a domain change.
cases.control: signed chain identifier and current chain identifier
cases.guard: Commit the current chain and verifying endpoint into the signed domain.
cases.invariant: A signature authorized for one chain domain must not authorize another chain domain.
sequence: submit identical signature bytes on chain 2

cases.applicability: Applies to adjacent attacker-controlled dynamic fields encoded without boundaries; fixed-width or canonical ABI encodings do not collide this way.
cases.attacker: A caller selecting two variable-length fields covered by an existing authorization.
cases.control: field boundaries in signed and requested tuples
cases.guard: Use canonical typed encoding with explicit lengths or fixed-width fields.
cases.invariant: Distinct typed field tuples must not share an authorization encoding.
sequence: request ('a','bc') with the same concatenated bytes

cases.applicability: Applies when external token decimals differ from the ledger scale and metadata reaches valuation; same-decimal assets are not a useful test of this precondition.
cases.attacker: A permissionless depositor selecting a token with 6 decimal places.
cases.guard: Normalize token units exactly once before applying the price.
cases.invariant: Minted debt units must not exceed the decimal-normalized collateral value.

cases.applicability: Applies where users can trigger repeated upward rounding before aggregation; one-shot settlement or downward rounding has different economics.
cases.attacker: An eligible claimant selecting the number of settlement rounds.
cases.control: partition count for a fixed numerator and denominator
cases.guard: Accumulate exact numerators and round once at the settlement boundary.
cases.invariant: Splitting one claim into rounds cannot increase its total integer payout.
sequence: split a 5/3 entitlement into three unit-numerator rounds

cases.applicability: Applies when multiple public handlers reach the same state transition with duplicated validation; a single shared validator removes the path divergence.
cases.attacker: A frozen account holder selecting the batch endpoint.
cases.guard: Apply the same account-state predicate to every transfer transition.
cases.invariant: Frozen accounts cannot transfer through any public transition path.
sequence: submit one transfer through batch instead of direct transfer

cases.applicability: Applies when conclusions about source are projected onto a separately built or deployed artifact; reproducible digest equality makes this case inapplicable.
cases.attacker: A permissionless caller reaching a stale deployment; no deployment privilege is assumed.
cases.guard: Verify deployed artifact digest against the reviewed build before assigning evidence class.
cases.invariant: The executable artifact must match the reviewed and declared release identifier.
sequence: invoke endpoint whose deployed artifact is still v1

cases.applicability: Models attacker-amplified linear work at an untrusted boundary; deployments with stricter transport limits below the verifier cap are not reachable this way.
cases.attacker: An unauthenticated peer supplying a syntactically valid oversized proof.
cases.guard: Reject proof cardinality above the consensus-safe cap before per-item work.
cases.invariant: A single untrusted proof cannot consume work above the protocol verification cap.
sequence: send it to the public verification path
